findings.location: tools/linux-appimage/tests/test-build-environment.sh lines 254-263 (only libssl ordering asserted); no check of the floor-check step
findings.obligation: Expected: the libssl rejection and the floor check stay between build and upload; P1: CI fails if a build exceeds the floor
findings.observation: Only the libssl step is ordered (build_line -lt libssl_line). No assertion names the step Reject an AppImage that needs a newer glibc than the floor, or check-glibc-floor.sh in the package job, or orders it against the build and the upload-artifact step. Deleting that step from the workflow passes every workflow check in the oracle.
findings.remediation: Add pass or fail checks: the floor-check step line is after the tauri-apps/tauri-action line and before the upload-artifact line; the libssl step is before the upload line. Use the file WHAT/WHY/HOW convention.

findings.obligation: Expected: the workflow prints the installed WebKitGTK version
findings.observation: Line 223 requires a dpkg-query or apt print on a line that does not contain apt-get install. Line 441 requires the version in the output of the install step, extracted by step_containing apt-get install. A print in a separate step passes 223 and fails 441 (install output lacks the version). A print on the apt-get install line fails 223. The two checks disagree on placement, so a valid candidate can be refused.
findings.remediation: Pick one placement and make both checks read it: for example require the dpkg-query print inside the install step and remove the grep -v exclusion at line 223, or run every run-script of the package job before the probe and compare its output. Keep the installed-version comparison.

findings.obligation: Expected: the ADR and the floor file exist and agree
findings.observation: Agreement is tested by has_text of the phrases Ubuntu 24.04 and glibc 2.39 over the ADR prose. Phrase presence over prose is a wording pin: a reworded ADR fails, and a stale ADR that keeps the phrases passes.
findings.remediation: Replace the phrase test with a machine fact: a structured floor and release line the ADR must carry, compared with tools/linux-appimage/glibc-floor, or drop the phrase test and keep the file-existence check.

findings.obligation: P3 and E5: the loader check is the semantic RED checkpoint before craft
findings.observation: check-loads-on.sh does not exist. Six loader cases and both finished-AppImage cases fail with exit 127 and No such file, not with a named missing-script failure. The checkpoint is indistinguishable from a broken fixture.
findings.remediation: Assert first that tools/linux-appimage/check-loads-on.sh is a regular file, with one WHAT/WHY/HOW failure naming it; then skip the dependent cases with that single failure instead of running them against nothing.
